curriculum.lesson_evidence: Planning a healthy meal means choosing foods from several groups and thinking about cost, time, allergies and what the family enjoys. Steps: decide the meal, list the foods by group, see what you already have, write a shopping list and note safe preparation steps. Adults help with sharp tools and hot items, and anyone with an allergy or medical need follows their own advice.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A family has a small shopping budget and one person with a nut allergy. Plan a protein food for the meal that avoids nuts.

FEEDBACK
Options: eggs, chicken, baked beans or fish. Always read labels for hidden nuts and follow medical advice. A good plan solves the problems (budget and allergy) while keeping variety.

WATCH FOR
Thinking a healthy meal is always expensive or hard to make. Simple foods such as beans, eggs, seasonal vegetables and oats can be affordable and healthy.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Plan one dinner for your household that includes at least four food groups. Write the menu by group, a shopping list, two safety steps for preparation and one way to adjust for anyone's food needs or allergies. Cook only with an adult.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teaching.model: Planning a healthy meal means choosing foods from several groups and thinking about cost, time, allergies and what the family enjoys. Steps: decide the meal, list the foods by group, see what you already have, write a shopping list and note safe preparation steps. Adults help with sharp tools and hot items, and anyone with an allergy or medical need follows their own advice. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
